bot_adx_v1.method:
Per research trade: value = notional_x * net_pct_11bp.
(1) net_pct_11bp = ledger net_pct + 0.04. The ledger net_pct is gross - 15 bp - funding paid (adx_lib.py:113). Adding 0.04 brings the cost to the 11 bp the live close books (10 fee + 1 slippage). The adjustment is exact because cost is linear in notional (trades.py:341-356). Funding stays in, signed (longs pay, shorts receive), charged over (entry_ts, exit_ts].
(2) notional_x is the live fixed-R rule, recomputed at each signal bar on the same 361-day truncated window the live loader returns (signal.py:59; 200 + WARMUP 151 + 10). stop_frac = min(0.10, 4*ATR14/close) (signal.py:531-536). notional = 10000*2%/stop_frac, capped at 3x (botlib.py:527-528). The result is 0.2000x on 13 of the 17 kept trades and 0.2003-0.2184x on the rest. The cap never binds. The live open trade SJ-4247 booked size_usdt 2000 = 0.2x, which agrees.
(3) Funding veto: every long's 30-day funding z is computed with the production _funding_z on the live window. Longs with z > 1.5 are dropped: 2020-07-28 (z 4.80), 2021-02-09 (2.83), 2025-07-16 (1.75) and 2025-10-05 (1.53, matching the parity test). Dropping them changes nothing else. All 22 signals in the window became trades, so no signal was ever suppressed by an open position, and was_low is used up regardless of the veto (signal.py:194, 505-514).
(4) Capital is a fixed $10k with no compounding (sizing reads variant capital_usdt).
(5) Order is chronological by exit. Only one position is open at a time, so exit order equals entry order.
Exit policy inherited from live_walk: ADX<20 at the UTC boundary (priced at the 1m close); a 10% fixed stop and an ATR(14)x4 trail that ratchets on closes, both checked minute by minute (a wick fills at the stop, a gap fills at the open); each day's trail level applies from the next day. Entry is at the first 1m close after the boundary. No cooldown exists beyond one decision per UTC day.
bot_adx_v1.caveats:
1) In-sample veto, so this reference is optimistic. The z>1.5 veto was chosen on 2026-06-27 by looking at these same trades, with 2025-10 as the target case (adx_study/findings.md addendum 2). Here it removes 4 losing longs worth -6.29 pp of capital in total. Without the veto (n=21, same window), the chronological values are [0.6985, 0.8758, -1.5717, 31.2456, -2.1122, -2.0994, 9.3681, -2.02, 0.9372, 0.985, -0.3237, -0.8657, 10.4938, 5.3155, -2.0313, 5.1944, 2.2307, -0.7617, -1.8432, 4.4324, 2.5369]: mean 2.890, win rate 57.1%. An optimistic reference makes the AMBER warning fire more easily.
2) The sample is tiny and heavily skewed. 17 trades over 6.6 years is about 2.6 per year. One trade (2020-10-17 long, +31.25%) is 47% of the summed result. Median 0.99, SD 7.96. Bootstrap p10 of resampled means (200k draws, veto set / no-veto set): n=1 -2.03/-2.03, n=2 -0.61/-1.44, n=3 -0.15/-0.99, n=5 +0.38/-0.36, n=10 +1.15/+0.32. The veto set's p10 is positive from n=5, so with only a few live trades the warning is decided mainly by whether a big trend winner has happened yet.
3) The fill model is the study's replica of live semantics, not live fills. The study showed it reproduces the harness to +/-1 pp CAGR once funding is excluded. It assumes the daily bar is final at 00:00 and the entry fills on the first minute. The late-entry audit found entering later costs at most 0.5 pp per trade at 6 h.
4) Funding uses the study's Binance settlement cache. Checked against production accrued_pct on cd_funding_rate: identical for all 21 trades to at least 3 decimals, and values match to 6 decimals.
5) Signal parity on the live loader's 361-day window: production _current_signal fires exactly the 21 ledger signals plus 2026-08-21 (the open live trade) and nothing else. EMA150 on the truncated window differs from full history by up to 1.1%, but no entry changed. ADX differs by at most 8e-9, so no ADX<20 exit changes.
6) Excludes 2018-2019: there is no btc_1m path, and no BTCUSDT perp funding exists before 2019-09.
7) Cross-check with adx_study harness.run(with_funding=True) (daily-bar fills, stop filled at its level, same-bar trail), cost adjusted 10 to 11 bp, same sizing and veto: 2020+ gives n=17, mean 3.936, win rate 70.6%. 2018+ gives n=23, mean 4.008 (4 trades carry zero funding). 2018+ without veto gives n=27, mean 3.165. The harness and the live-semantics ledger agree.
8) No overlap with live results: bot_adx_v1 has 0 closed trades as of 2026-09-14. The last research trade (short 2026-06-01 to 2026-08-08) was held live by the legacy variant p300_aggressive_v2_v1_0 (SJ-3821), not by this bot.
bot_adx_v1.notes:
One live variant: bot_adx_v1 (bots/adx/config.py:10). The main source is the adx_robustness_2026_09 live-semantics ledger rather than harness.run(with_funding=True). It copies the live bot more closely: entry on the first minute after the boundary, stops checked minute by minute, the trail applied from the next day, and Binance settlement funding on every trade. The harness, by contrast, fills on daily bars and has no funding before 2019-09. I still ran the harness with funding as a cross-check (caveat 7), and on the 2020+ window it gives the same mean to 0.004 pp.

The live bot books 11 bp, funding, and a notional of about 0.2x capital (2% risk over a 10% stop), so each value is roughly 0.2 x the per-trade net % of notional.

Main judgement call for the dashboard owner: the live bot runs the funding-crowding long veto, so the returned distribution applies it. That veto was fitted in-sample on these very trades. It removes 4 losers and lifts the mean from 2.89 to 3.94 % of capital; the no-veto values are listed in caveat 1 if a more conservative reference is preferred.

The distribution is small (n=17) and dominated by one +31% trend trade. Resampled-mean p10 is negative for n<=3 and positive from about n=5 (caveat 2). The bot averages about 2.6 trades a year and has no closed live trades yet, so the warning will stay statistically weak for years.
